summary: Embed dimension negotiation: proxy strips metadata header causing rerank CPU fallback and intermittent empty results
description:
Issue summary: Since 2026-03-11 22:00 UTC, CortexSearch reports intermittent empty candidate sets and p95 rerank latency spikes for their dedicated pool. The symptoms started shortly after they flipped the proxy compression/fast-path toggle during a traffic spike.

Impact: Client-facing search experiences occasional blank results and multi-second tail latency for rerank calls affecting approx 2-3% of queries; revenue impact unknown but noticeable on monitoring dashboards.

Environment: Dedicated cluster in us-west, vpc-connected private control plane, embed endpoint pinned to embed-small-v2, rerank endpoint pinned to rerank-lite-v1.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send embed request with Accept: application/x-embed+proto and X-Embed-Dims: 128 to /v1/embeddings
2) Immediately call rerank with the returned embedding payload to /v1/rerank
3) Observe sometimes an empty candidate list and/or rerank p95 > 1.2s

Expected behavior: Rerank accepts the embedding payload and returns top candidates within SLOs.

Actual behavior: Around 2-3% of requests the rerank returns an empty set and the request falls back to CPU ANN path, increasing latency; logs show that the rerank service sees embedding dimension header missing for those requests.

Logs/observations: Proxy access logs show some requests are rewritten by the fast-path compressor and drop custom headers (Accept and X-Embed-Dims). Reproducer snippet attached by customer shows payload intact but missing the X-Embed-Dims header when it reaches the rerank node.

Temporary customer workaround requested: disable proxy fast-path or pin embed to explicit wire-format variant that includes embedded-dim metadata in the payload body.
comments: 2026-03-12 08:14 - Support (Ava Chen): Thanks for the report, CortexSearch. We're triaging. Can you confirm whether you saw any proxy config changes around 22:00 UTC? Also requested a HAR and minimal repro payload.

2026-03-12 09:02 - CortexSearch (Arjun Patel): Confirmed — we toggled proxy compression fast-path to true at ~21:58 UTC to workaround some small spike. Attached HAR and repro script. Repro rate is ~1 in 40 requests locally against your dedicated endpoint.

2026-03-12 12:30 - SRE (Diego Morales): Observed matching symptom on dedicated ingress: Nginx sidecar combined with compressor module is dropping non-standard headers when the fast-path is enabled. Captured tcpdump showing header absent post-proxy before hitting rerank. Queued for infra patch.

2026-03-12 14:05 - Eng (Priya Rao): Hypothesis: proxy compression optimization strips custom headers with Accept-like names when using streaming chunking. Workaround: add X-Embed-Dims to preserved_headers list or switch to embedding payload embedding-dim in proto body. We'll prepare a small patch and a canary rollout to a single node pool.

2026-03-13 07:20 - Support (Ava Chen): Customer applied workaround to disable fast-path; reported immediate reduction in empty-results and improved p95. Still investigating root cause and patch schedule.

2026-03-14 10:45 - Infra (Diego Morales): Deployed infra PR to add X-Embed-Dims and other embed headers to preserved_headers list in the compressor. Canary scheduled on 2026-03-14 15:00 UTC for one node in us-west dedicated pool.
2026-03-14 17:30 - CortexSearch (Arjun Patel): Canary looks good so far; no empty results for last 10k queries. Please advise ETA to roll to full pool and recommended long-term mitigation.

2026-03-14 17:45 - Eng (Priya Rao): Plan: merge infra PR, release serving-runtime change to treat missing header as reject (fail-fast) to avoid silent CPU fallback while we rollout. Full rollout planned 2026-03-15 if canary remains stable.
2026-03-14 17:55 - Support (Ava Chen): Noted. Customer asked for retro/postmortem once complete and for a runbook entry. Assigned follow-ups to ENG and SRE teams.
investigation_notes: Captured tcpdump and sidecar logs showing header present at client -> proxy boundary but absent proxy -> server for affected requests.
Compressor fast-path uses streaming chunking optimization that re-encodes headers; test harness reproduced header strip when Accept-like header names used.
Rerank service logic currently tolerates missing dimension header and falls back to ANN CPU path instead of rejecting; this leads to silent quality/latency regressions.
Repro rate correlates with specific payload sizes and alignment with compressor chunk size (edge cases when embedding payload crosses chunk boundary).
No evidence of payload corruption; only header loss. Customer payload body still contains serialized vector in all cases.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied: Customer disabled proxy fast-path (immediate fix) and observed elimination of empty candidate cases.
Infra fix: PR merged to preserve embed-related headers (X-Embed-Dims, X-Embed-Proto, X-Embed-Checksum) across compressor fast-path. Canary rolled at 2026-03-14 15:00 UTC with no regressions observed.

Serving runtime change: added defensive validation to rerank service to fail-fast with 400 if required embedding metadata header is missing instead of silently falling back to CPU ANN. This avoids silent quality regressions; rolled to canary concurrently.

Planned rollout: full rollout to dedicated pools on 2026-03-15 pending monitoring. Post-deploy, will push a Confluence runbook entry and update API docs recommending embedding-dimension included in payload body for extra safety.
Follow-ups: create INT ticket to audit other custom headers that may be stripped (INT-2021 linked). Customer requested a short postmortem and confirmation once full rollout completes.
